question: Which body systems work together to create coordinated movement?

options.A: Musculoskeletal and nervous systems
options.B: Cardiovascular and lymphatic systems
options.C: Respiratory and endocrine systems
options.D: Digestive and urinary systems

explanation: Movement requires the structural support of bones and muscles directed and coordinated by the nervous system. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why does eating a fatty meal trigger severe pain in someone with gallstones?

options.A: Stomach acid mixes with fat to create a toxic gas.
options.B: The liver swells instantly from eating too much oil.
options.C: The gallbladder contracts to release bile against blocked stones.
options.D: Fat directly irritates the lining of the stomach.

explanation: When fat hits the small intestine, your gallbladder squeezes to send out bile. If gallstones are blocking the path, that squeeze causes sharp pain!

question: What is the main reason lab scientists perform a crossmatch before releasing blood?

options.A: To check for hidden antibodies and ensure true compatibility between donor and recipient
options.B: To determine the patient's exact height and weight for dosage calculations
options.C: To sterilize the blood product before it leaves the blood bank
options.D: To measure the exact volume of red blood cells in the donor bag

explanation: Crossmatching is like a test-drive in a test tube! It mixes donor cells with patient serum to catch any immune clashes early.

question: What are two major health issues strongly linked with a high BMI in the obesity range?

options.A: Hyperthyroidism and rapid muscle growth
options.B: Osteoporosis and iron deficiency anemia
options.C: Type 2 diabetes and hypertension
options.D: Insomnia and chronic low blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Carrying extra weight puts extra strain on the body's systems, making conditions like type 2 diabetes and high blood pressure much more likely.

question: What is the frontline medication used to treat schistosomiasis?

options.A: Albendazole
options.B: Metronidazole
options.C: Praziquantel
options.D: Artemether

explanation: Praziquantel is the trusty, WHO-recommended drug used worldwide to clear up this infection. Bookmark this drug name—you'll see it often in exams!

question: What is the main goal of a surgical hand scrub compared to a normal quick wash?

options.A: To greatly reduce germ numbers and stop them from multiplying
options.B: To completely get rid of all germs on the skin
options.C: To wash away visible dirt with plain soap
options.D: To permanently kill all sweat glands

explanation: You've got this! Germs live deep in our skin and can never be completely wiped out, so our goal is to lower their numbers and keep them from growing.

question: What is the primary role of natural anticoagulants like antithrombin III?

options.A: To prevent unwanted clotting in healthy, uninjured blood vessels
options.B: To stimulate platelets to stick together during a vascular injury
options.C: To dissolve large clots that have already formed in the legs
options.D: To speed up the conversion of fibrinogen into solid fibrin

explanation: Natural anticoagulants keep the clotting system in check so that blood does not form dangerous clots where there is no injury. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T3#GNS111_U2_T3_h6)

question: What triggers a tapeworm cyst to release its head (scolex) once a human eats contaminated meat?

options.A: Gastric acid and enzymes digesting the cyst wall to release the scolex
options.B: Immune system suppression caused by the larval waste products
options.C: The low temperature inside the human small intestine
options.D: Direct contact with human blood cells in the mucosal lining

explanation: Exactly! Stomach acid and digestive juices break open the cyst, freeing the scolex so it can attach firmly to the small intestine.

question: What is the primary purpose of presenting data in nursing research?

options.A: To make raw information easy to understand and use
options.B: To replace the need for written conclusions
options.C: To make research articles longer and more academic
options.D: To hide errors in clinical measurements

explanation: Presenting data organizes chaotic raw information into a clear format so readers can easily grasp clinical findings. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T6#GNS217_U4_T6_h1)

question: A healthy family member who was exposed to measles is asked to stay at home and avoid contact with others for a short period. What is this control measure called?

options.A: Quarantine
options.B: Isolation
options.C: Active immunization
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: You got it! Quarantine is used for healthy people who were exposed, to watch if they develop symptoms, whereas isolation is for people who are already sick.

question: What is the single most powerful way to stop infections from spreading during patient care?

options.A: Wearing a heavy surgical gown
options.B: Changing bed sheets twice a day
options.C: Spraying the room with chemicals
options.D: Washing your hands properly

explanation: You nailed it! Clean hands are your best defense. Washing before and after care stops germs right in their tracks.

question: What is a great food tip for a patient who feels nauseated and has a poor appetite during cancer treatment?

options.A: Eat three large heavy meals at traditional times
options.B: Offer small, frequent meals that are high in protein
options.C: Avoid all protein and eat only plain white sugar
options.D: Eat food straight from the oven while it is piping hot and aromatic

explanation: Large meals can overwhelm a weak tummy. Small, protein-rich snacks are much easier to handle and help keep their strength up!

question: What is a main duty of Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs) in a PHC clinic?

options.A: Performing major specialized surgical operations independently
options.B: Managing hospital-wide administrative budgets and procurement
options.C: Handling international health policy formulation and funding
options.D: Diagnosing and treating minor ailments using standing orders

explanation: CHEWs are superstars at the community level! They use approved standing orders to treat common issues like malaria safely and quickly.

question: What is the main goal of disaster preparedness in nursing?

options.A: To entirely prevent natural disasters from occurring in local communities
options.B: To reduce the financial operational costs of running a public hospital
options.C: To ensure a rapid and effective clinical response when a crisis strikes
options.D: To punish staff who fail to report for emergency duty shifts

explanation: You've got this! Preparedness is all about taking smart steps before a crisis hits so our healthcare teams can jump in quickly and save lives when emergencies happen.

question: Through which pathway do surgeons typically reach the pituitary gland during a transsphenoidal hypophysectomy?

options.A: Through a large incision made just above the right ear
options.B: Through a small opening cut directly in the upper jawbone
options.C: Through the nasal cavity and the sphenoid sinus
options.D: Through the back of the neck right near the brainstem

explanation: The 'transsphenoidal' approach means going right through the nose and sphenoid sinus! This lets surgeons reach the pituitary safely without having to cut open the skull or go through brain tissue.

question: Why does HIV rely on the enzyme reverse transcriptase once it enters a host cell?

options.A: To cut open the host cell membrane
options.B: To repair damaged viral genetic material
options.C: To destroy competing white blood cells
options.D: To convert viral RNA into DNA

explanation: Think of reverse transcriptase as a translator. It changes the virus's RNA into DNA so the instructions can blend right into the host cell's own chromosomes!

question: Why is it important to include a data analysis plan in your research proposal?

options.A: To allow the hospital pharmacy to order more medication supplies
options.B: To calculate the exact travel expenses of the research team
options.C: To ensure that no patients ever experience physical pain
options.D: To prove that the collected data can actually answer the research questions

explanation: Showing your analysis plan ahead of time proves your study is well-thought-out and that your results will actually answer your research questions.

question: What is the foramen ovale?

options.A: A valve inside the umbilical cord
options.B: An opening between the right and left atria
options.C: A vessel connecting the liver to the heart
options.D: An artery carrying blood to the placenta

explanation: The foramen ovale is a hole in the heart wall separating the upper chambers, letting blood cross straight over. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h3)

question: When one mature cell type changes into another mature cell type due to ongoing irritation, what is it called?

options.A: Anaplasia
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Apoptosis

explanation: Spot on! Metaplasia is like a cellular makeover; cells switch to a tougher type to better handle chronic stress, such as smoke irritation in the airways.

question: Why do healthcare workers often resist new changes introduced in the hospital?

options.A: Fear of the unknown and disruption to established routines
options.B: A lack of interest in improving patient care quality
options.C: Federal laws prohibiting changes to shift schedules
options.D: Desire to challenge the authority of the nursing director

explanation: Change can feel scary because it disrupts familiar habits. Good leaders understand this and communicate clearly to support their team through it.

question: What does gender-based violence (GBV) mean in simple terms?

options.A: Any harmful act directed against someone based on their gender
options.B: Accidental injuries sustained during high-contact sports
options.C: Physical fights that happen exclusively between married couples
options.D: Violent crimes committed only against adult males in public spaces

explanation: You've got this! GBV is any harmful act forced on someone simply because of their gender. It stems from unequal power and societal expectations. Keep up the great work!

question: What is a common misconception about mental illness that fuels community stigma?

options.A: Knowing that counseling and medication help recovery
options.B: Believing it is caused by curses, witchcraft, or personal moral failure
options.C: Understanding it as a treatable medical condition affecting brain chemistry
options.D: Recognizing that stress can trigger episodes in anyone

explanation: False beliefs attributing mental illness to supernatural curses or weakness often lead to harsh discrimination and delay proper medical treatment. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h6)

question: Why is local health research important for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Foreign textbooks are too expensive for local nursing students to buy
options.B: International organizations pay large grants exclusively to clinical nurses
options.C: Nigerian hospitals require every nurse to publish a paper before promotion
options.D: Western guidelines do not address specific local health challenges and cultural realities

explanation: You've got this! Local research matters because health issues like malaria management and maternal care need solutions tailored to our environment, rather than just copying foreign data. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which sign strongly suggests a pregnant woman's uterus has ruptured during a difficult labor?

options.A: A gradual increase in contractions with steady pink show
options.B: Sudden sharp tearing pain and disappearance of contractions
options.C: High fever accompanied by foul-smelling vaginal discharge
options.D: Mild lower backache that improves when walking around

explanation: If contractions suddenly stop after a sharp, tearing pain, think uterine rupture. It's a major emergency!

question: A nurse is caring for a patient recovering from major surgery. Who is the best healthcare professional to consult for a custom diet plan?

options.A: Physical therapist
options.B: Biomedical technician
options.C: Registered dietitian
options.D: Hospital pharmacist

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Dietitians are the absolute experts at calculating precise calories and nutrients for patients who need special nutritional healing.

question: You are reviving a woman with severe shock from bleeding. What size of IV cannula should you secure first?

options.A: 22-gauge green cannula
options.B: 24-gauge yellow cannula
options.C: 16-gauge or 18-gauge large-bore cannula
options.D: 26-gauge tiny pediatric cannula

explanation: You got it! Large-bore cannulas let fluids and blood flow in rapidly when treating severe shock. In an emergency, bigger is definitely better!

question: What life stage is second only to infancy regarding the speed of physical growth?

options.A: Toddlerhood
options.B: Middle childhood
options.C: Adolescence
options.D: Young adulthood

explanation: Teenagers undergo a major growth spurt that rivals infancy in speed and nutritional demand. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h1)

question: Where should your finished knot sit after tying a simple interrupted stitch?

options.A: Tucked tightly underneath the tissue forceps
options.B: Off to the side of the incision line
options.C: Buried deep underneath the subcutaneous fat layer
options.D: Directly in the center of the open wound gap

explanation: Always pull your knot off to the side! This keeps it from pressing down directly into the healing cut and causing irritation. Perfect technique!

question: What triggers the physical changes of puberty?

options.A: Hormonal surges from the endocrine system
options.B: Sudden changes in environmental temperature
options.C: Rapid expansion of skeletal muscle mass
options.D: Increased intake of dietary proteins

explanation: Puberty kicks off when the brain sends signals to the endocrine system to release hormones that drive body changes.

question: Which of the following is an example of health advocacy by a nurse?

options.A: Refusing to care for patients from different tribes
options.B: Prescribing antibiotics independently without a doctor
options.C: Keeping all hospital supply records a strict secret
options.D: Speaking up about dangerous staff shortages on the ward

explanation: Advocacy involves defending patient safety and speaking out against systemic issues that compromise care quality. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h7)

question: What does consumer purchasing power refer to?

options.A: The physical strength of shoppers carrying heavy bags from the market
options.B: The financial ability of a household to buy goods and services with their income
options.C: The political influence grocery store chains have over food pricing laws
options.D: The total amount of food a farmer can produce in a single season

explanation: Purchasing power measures what an individual or family can actually afford to buy with available funds. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for preventing harm from gishiri cuts?

options.A: Providing emergency obstetric services
options.B: Expanding access to skilled antenatal care
options.C: Community health education on pelvic anatomy
options.D: Training traditional birth attendants to perform safer cuts

explanation: The goal is to stop the practice entirely rather than make cutting safer, as the procedure itself lacks any medical validity. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h7)

question: Which of these choices is a MAJOR safety violation when handling hospital equipment?

options.A: Checking for frayed electrical cords
options.B: Obtaining informed consent from the patient
options.C: Skipping equipment cleaning to save time
options.D: Ensuring proper disinfection between patients

explanation: Never skip cleaning! Proper maintenance and disinfection protect patients from nasty infections and keep equipment running smoothly.

question: Your patient just had surgery and has painful trapped gas. What is the best first nursing action?

options.A: Insert a rigid nasogastric tube immediately without a doctor's order.
options.B: Assist the patient to ambulate in the hallway or change positions in bed.
options.C: Instruct the patient to hold the gas in to prevent embarrassment.
options.D: Administer strong intravenous narcotics for pain relief.

explanation: Movement is medicine! Getting a post-op patient walking or shifting positions wakes up the bowels and helps release gas naturally.

question: Why is removing patient names and personal details (de-identifying) so important in chart review studies?

options.A: To protect patient privacy and confidentiality
options.B: To satisfy financial auditors from the hospital
options.C: To prevent missing data from appearing in the results
options.D: To make the data collection process go much faster

explanation: You got it! Patient confidentiality is sacred in nursing. Stripping away names ensures nobody's private medical history is exposed during your research.

question: Which of these is a main dietary goal for preventing lifestyle diseases?

options.A: Eliminating all forms of protein from meals
options.B: Reducing excessive salt and sugar intake
options.C: Doubling daily caloric consumption
options.D: Eating only imported canned foods

explanation: Spot on! Cutting down on too much salt and sugar is a powerful way to help prevent conditions like hypertension, obesity, and diabetes.

question: What is the main goal of Directly Observed Therapy (DOT) for TB patients?

options.A: Reducing the overall financial cost of purchasing prescription drugs
options.B: Eliminating the need for periodic sputum laboratory testing
options.C: Ensuring patients swallow every medication dose to prevent resistance
options.D: Allowing nurses to monitor daily lung function and oxygen saturation

explanation: With DOT, a health worker watches the patient take their drugs. This stops missed doses and prevents drug-resistant TB strains from forming.

question: Why is it so important for you as a nurse to understand how a community functions?

options.A: To prescribe medications without needing a doctor
options.B: To manage hospital financial budgets and staff salaries
options.C: To understand how daily living conditions affect people's health
options.D: To diagnose rare genetic diseases in hospital laboratories

explanation: Spot on! The environment and everyday resources around your patients shape their health just as much as any medicine you give them.

question: What does a normal P wave tell us on an ECG?

options.A: Sudden failure of the aortic valve
options.B: Electrical activation of the atria
options.C: Complete relaxation of the whole heart
options.D: Dangerous blockage in a coronary artery

explanation: The little P wave is just the atria waking up and squeezing blood down to the ventricles. Easy peasy!

question: A hospital wants to check if their new nurse-led clinic actually lowered stroke rates over the past 5 years. What type of activity is this?

options.A: Evaluation, because it looks at long-term outcomes and overall impact
options.B: Monitoring, because it tracks daily blood pressure checks
options.C: Budgeting, because it calculates the cost of stethoscopes
options.D: Auditing, because it checks if nurses sign patient charts

explanation: Looking back over several years to see if health truly improved is a big-picture evaluation, not just daily monitoring.

question: Which hormone is mostly responsible for relaxing smooth muscles during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Spot on! Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles everywhere in the body, which is why digestion slows down and blood vessels change.

question: What is the main difference between a normal fear and a phobia?

options.A: A phobia only happens during sleep
options.B: A normal fear never causes physical symptoms
options.C: A normal fear lasts for many years
options.D: A phobia is out of proportion to any actual danger

explanation: Phobias involve an extreme and irrational reaction that does not match the real level of threat present. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h1)

question: How does a night hospital typically work for its clients?

options.A: Clients visit only for medication administration once a week at midnight
options.B: Clients sleep at the facility at night and work or attend school during the day
options.C: Clients receive therapy all night and sleep at home during the day
options.D: Clients stay locked in the ward 24 hours a day with weekend leave

explanation: You got it! Night hospitals provide a safe place to sleep overnight so clients can still go about their normal daytime routines.

question: Why is checking for malnutrition important before a patient goes for surgery?

options.A: It shortens the time the patient spends in the recovery room
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any intravenous fluids
options.C: It ensures the patient will never feel nauseated after waking up
options.D: It helps the body withstand surgical stress and prevents complications

explanation: Spot on! Well-nourished patients handle the stress of an operation much better and have a lower risk of infections.

question: Why do nurses need to understand basic physical therapy principles?

options.A: To reinforce exercises during daily patient care activities
options.B: To diagnose musculoskeletal disorders independently
options.C: To replace the work of physical therapists on the ward
options.D: To prescribe new rehabilitation programs for patients

explanation: You spend the most time with patients on the ward! By understanding these basics, you can help patients keep up with their exercises while doing normal daily care.

question: Where do the main coronary arteries start from?

options.A: The left ventricle
options.B: The superior vena cava
options.C: The ascending aorta
options.D: The pulmonary artery

explanation: Great job! The coronary arteries branch off right at the base of the ascending aorta, just above the aortic valve, so they can grab freshly oxygenated blood first thing.

question: Why is it a must to check a patient's blood glucose level before injecting the PET tracer?

options.A: Insulin production stops completely once the radioactive dye enters veins.
options.B: Low blood sugar causes immediate cardiac arrest inside the scanner.
options.C: High blood sugar competes with the tracer and ruins the image quality.
options.D: Elevated glucose levels neutralize the radioactivity of the tracer.

explanation: Spot on! If there is too much normal sugar in the blood, the cells will eat that instead of our FDG tracer, and the scan pictures will turn out blurry or misleading.

question: How soon can a person start ovulating again after experiencing an abortion?

options.A: As early as two weeks
options.B: Only after a full year passes
options.C: Never, fertility is permanently lost
options.D: After exactly six months

explanation: Correct! Fertility can return surprisingly fast—sometimes in just two weeks—which is why talking about contraception early is so crucial.

question: When is the best time for a nurse to document that a medication was given?

options.A: While walking down the hallway to the room
options.B: Right before taking the pills out of the drawer
options.C: At the very end of the entire work shift
options.D: Immediately after the patient swallows the drug

explanation: Documenting right away prevents accidental double-dosing and ensures an accurate record of care. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h3)

question: Which physical sign makes a nurse suspect non-accidental trauma?

options.A: A scratch on the cheek from a household pet
options.B: Injuries found in various stages of healing
options.C: A small bruise on the shin of a toddler
options.D: A scraped knee from falling off a bicycle

explanation: When bruises or fractures are healing at different times, it usually points to repeated, intentional harm instead of a normal fall.

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of circulatory overload during a blood transfusion?

options.A: Shortness of breath and crackles in the lungs
options.B: Sudden widespread hives and severe skin itching
options.C: High fever accompanied by uncontrollable shivering
options.D: Sharp pain radiating into the lower back area

explanation: Circulatory overload occurs when fluid volume overwhelms the heart, leading to pulmonary congestion and breathing difficulty. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which phase of the menstrual cycle comes immediately after ovulation?

options.A: The luteal phase
options.B: The menstrual phase
options.C: The proliferative phase
options.D: The follicular phase

explanation: Right after ovulation, the cycle enters the luteal phase. This is when the leftover follicle forms the corpus luteum to produce progesterone.

question: Why do we usually need to treat everyone in a household if just one person has pinworms?

options.A: Healthy people absorb extra nutrition from the medication
options.B: Insurance companies require every family member to take pills
options.C: Pinworms spread easily among people living in close contact
options.D: The drug loses its potency if not shared by a group

explanation: You nailed it! Pinworm eggs pass around so easily on hands, sheets, and dust that everyone in the house will likely just pass it back and forth if not treated together.

question: What is the main purpose of triage during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: To distribute financial relief funds to displaced families
options.B: To sort patients based on injury severity to prioritize critical care
options.C: To register patients for national health insurance policies
options.D: To assess structural damage to hospital buildings

explanation: Triage lets nurses and doctors quickly assess victims so that those with life-threatening injuries get treated first. You'll master this in clinicals! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h8)

question: What is the main goal of a cerebral angiography test?

options.A: To drain extra fluid from the brain ventricles
options.B: To measure electrical activity in the brain
options.C: To check the bone thickness at the skull base
options.D: To visualize blood vessels and spot aneurysms or blockages

explanation: Angiography uses dye to map out the brain's blood vessels, helping find narrow spots or weak bulging areas.

question: Why do heavy workloads and staff fatigue make patient harm more likely?

options.A: They strain cognitive resources and make workers prone to lapses in attention
options.B: They legally exempt hospitals from following standard infection control
options.C: They prevent nurses from documenting vital signs on paper charts
options.D: They automatically guarantee that physicians will order incorrect lab tests

explanation: You nailed it! When nurses or doctors are exhausted and stressed, their mental focus drops, making it easier to miss important clinical signs.

question: What is the main use of a partograph during active labor?

options.A: To record the financial bills accrued by the patient
options.B: To track the progress of labor and spot deviations early
options.C: To schedule the exact minute the baby will be born
options.D: To calculate the exact birth weight of the baby beforehand

explanation: Spot on! The partograph gives a clear picture of how labor is going, helping us catch any trouble early.

question: Which nursing check is most critical immediately after a patient returns from a tubal ligation procedure?

options.A: Assessing the client's ability to conceive within one month
options.B: Testing the patient for signs of future fertility recovery
options.C: Measuring exact daily caloric intake and urinary output
options.D: Monitoring vital signs and assessing the abdominal incision site

explanation: Immediate post-operative care centers on recovery from anesthesia, stable vital signs, and watching for bleeding or complications at the surgical site. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of health education in schools?

options.A: To help students adopt and maintain healthy lifestyle behaviors
options.B: To train students to administer prescription drugs
options.C: To replace traditional biology and science classes
options.D: To diagnose complex medical disorders in children

explanation: Correct! Health education is all about giving students practical knowledge to build good, lifelong personal habits.

question: How is genuine trust primarily built in a nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: Through consistency, competence, and reliability
options.B: Through expensive gifts given to the household
options.C: By making quick promises that cannot be kept
options.D: By ignoring family members during home visits

explanation: Exactly! Trust takes time. Showing up ready, knowing your skills, and keeping your word is how you earn a patient's confidence.

question: Where do water-soluble hormones usually find their receptors?

options.A: On the outer cell surface
options.B: Inside the cell nucleus
options.C: Inside the mitochondrial matrix
options.D: Floating freely in the blood

explanation: Because water-soluble hormones can't slip right through the oily cell membrane, they latch onto receptors sitting on the outside of the cell to pass their message along! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T11#GNS211_U1_T11_h1)

question: What vital instruction must you give a patient who is taking prescribed corticosteroid therapy?

options.A: Double the dose whenever you feel stressed
options.B: Never stop taking the medication abruptly
options.C: Take the pills only once a month
options.D: Stop the drug immediately if you gain weight

explanation: You got it! Stopping steroids suddenly can shock the body because the adrenal glands go to sleep while on the medication. They must be tapered off slowly.

question: Which of these is a helpful harm-reduction tip for a patient who chooses to drink alcohol?

options.A: Eating a substantial meal before drinking to help slow down alcohol absorption
options.B: Driving home immediately after finishing the last drink to test reflexes
options.C: Replacing all water intake with high-strength spirits to build immunity
options.D: Consuming alcohol exclusively on an empty stomach to speed up digestion

explanation: Food in the tummy slows down how fast alcohol gets into the bloodstream, helping prevent a sudden, overwhelming spike in drunkenness.

question: Why do cities usually record higher family planning use than rural villages?

options.A: Better access to equipped health facilities and higher literacy
options.B: Rural health workers refuse to distribute any commodities
options.C: Contraceptives are strictly forbidden by law in villages
options.D: Traditional beliefs are completely absent in big cities

explanation: Being close to clinics and having better access to health education makes it much easier for city residents to get and use family planning services.

question: What does an odds ratio of greater than 1 tell us?

options.A: The exposure is a risk factor for the disease
options.B: There is no association between exposure and disease
options.C: The exposure protects against the disease
options.D: The study results are completely invalid

explanation: Brilliant! An odds ratio above 1 means the exposure showed up more often in the sick group, pointing to it as a potential risk factor.

question: At what point in the hospital workflow should waste segregation take place?

options.A: Inside the municipal waste truck during transit to the dump site
options.B: At the final incineration plant before burning begins
options.C: At the exact point of origin where the waste is generated
options.D: By the sanitary inspectors during their weekly hospital visits

explanation: Spot on! Sorting must happen immediately at the bedside or treatment area so hazardous and general waste never mix. Brilliant!

question: Why is strict confidentiality vital during family planning sessions?

options.A: It builds trust and encourages clients to seek needed care safely
options.B: It guarantees that the government will fund the clinic supplies
options.C: It prevents hospital administrators from auditing patient records
options.D: It stops family members from asking about the client's health

explanation: Clients need assurance that their private reproductive health details will not be shared openly in the community. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T022#GNS226_U6_T022_h2)

question: In the nursing process, what is the evaluation step used to find out?

options.A: Which nurse gets assigned to night shift duty
options.B: Whether patient goals and outcomes have been met
options.C: How much the patient's hospital bill will cost
options.D: What medications the doctor should prescribe next

explanation: Evaluation is your final check in the nursing process to see if your care plan actually helped the patient reach their health goals.

question: What is the main goal of nursing care for a patient at the end of life?

options.A: Preventing all family visits
options.B: Promoting comfort and dignity
options.C: Curing the underlying disease
options.D: Speeding up the dying process

explanation: When a disease cannot be cured, nursing care shifts its focus to keeping the patient comfortable and maintaining their dignity. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h1)

question: What is the purpose of the 'teach-back' method in home care?

options.A: Allowing the nurse to grade the family's cleaning skills
options.B: Checking if the patient or caregiver truly understands instructions
options.C: Testing the patient's ability to read a textbook out loud
options.D: Teaching the nurse how to use home appliances

explanation: Instead of asking 'Do you understand?', you ask them to explain the instructions back to you in their own words. It's a game-changer for safety!

question: A client is discharged after an abortion without a birth control method and fails to return for her two-week checkup. What major risk does she face?

options.A: A permanent inability to ever produce estrogen again
options.B: An unintended repeat pregnancy due to early ovulation
options.C: Severe weight loss from sudden hormonal withdrawal
options.D: An automatic infection in the uterine lining

explanation: Missing the follow-up without a started method leaves a gap in protection during a time when fertility has already returned. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h3)

question: A patient comes in with ringworm, a skin condition that loves warm and damp places. Which class of pathogen is causing this?

options.A: Bacterium
options.B: Protozoa
options.C: Fungus
options.D: Virus

explanation: Fungi love warm, humid places (just like our weather sometimes!). They are notorious for causing superficial skin issues like ringworm and athlete's foot.

question: Why do we keep a patient with a suspected spinal injury flat on a hard board?

options.A: To make it easier to slide them into the back of an ambulance
options.B: To reduce the overall weight of the patient during lifting
options.C: To allow the nurse to check the abdomen more frequently
options.D: To prevent twisting or bending of the spinal column

explanation: Exactly right! A rigid board stops any accidental bending that could cause permanent damage to the spinal cord.

question: What should a nurse do immediately if they spot a break in sterile technique?

options.A: Report the contamination and replace the compromised item immediately
options.B: Ignore it if nobody else saw it happen
options.C: Wipe the contaminated instrument with an alcohol swab and keep using it
options.D: Wait until the surgery is completely finished before mentioning it

explanation: Spot on! Patient safety comes first always. Never sweep a contamination under the rug—speak up and swap it out right away.

question: Which of these is NOT considered a stakeholder in a rural community immunization program?

options.A: Local religious leaders supporting health messaging
options.B: Mothers bringing their infants to the clinic
options.C: A pharmaceutical manufacturing company located overseas
options.D: Local government health department officials

explanation: Stakeholders are the people right there on the ground who care about or are affected by the program. An overseas factory making the drugs is just a distant supplier!

question: Which of these signs is the classic giveaway that an IV has 'infiltrated' (leaked into the tissue)?

options.A: A warm, red, hard streak running all the way up the arm
options.B: Severe chest pain accompanied by audible lung crackles
options.C: Bright red bleeding gushing out around the plastic catheter
options.D: Swelling, coolness, and pallor around the insertion site

explanation: Spot on! When IV fluid leaks into the tissue instead of the vein, it makes the skin look pale, feel cool, and swell up. Time to restart the line!

question: Who has the primary legal duty to provide a safe working environment in a hospital?

options.A: The pharmaceutical companies supplying hospital medications
options.B: The individual nursing students on clinical placement
options.C: The patients admitted to the medical and surgical wards
options.D: The hospital management and institutional administration

explanation: Management is legally required to give you safe facilities, working gear, and proper protection so you can do your job without undue risk.

question: The QA committee notices nurses are struggling with children's drug dosage calculations. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Wait until a patient gets harmed before taking action
options.B: Stop giving all drugs to children immediately
options.C: Suspend all nurses working in the children's ward
options.D: Organize training workshops and provide clear dosing charts

explanation: Great choice! When knowledge gaps pop up, the best fix is always supportive education and helpful tools.

question: What do we call it when a hospital ward slowly slips back into old, messy habits after an improvement project finishes?

options.A: Systemic clinical drift
options.B: Relapse to old ways
options.C: Forcing function failure
options.D: Special cause variation

explanation: It's easy to slide back into comfort zones! That's why keeping new habits alive requires ongoing teamwork and support.

question: Which breathing sound is a classic red flag for respiratory involvement in anaphylaxis?

options.A: Wheezing and stridor
options.B: Persistent dry cough
options.C: Absent breath sounds
options.D: Slow, shallow breathing

explanation: When airways swell up (stridor) and spasm (wheezing), air has a hard time getting through. This is an urgent airway warning!

question: Which of these is NOT a good idea if you are facing backlash or resistance for your advocacy work?

options.A: Building strong community alliances
options.B: Relying strictly on verified factual data
options.C: Collaborating with professional nursing bodies
options.D: Acting completely alone without informing anyone

explanation: Correct! Trying to fight battles all by yourself puts you at high risk. True safety and strength always come from teamwork and professional support.

question: While checking a patient's reflexes, you notice their knee-jerk reaction is unusually jumpy and hyperactive. What might this point toward?

options.A: A severed sensory skin receptor
options.B: A normal physiological variant requiring no note
options.C: Complete destruction of the muscle effector
options.D: An upper motor neuron lesion

explanation: Great clinical thinking! When the brain's upper motor neurons lose their normal calming grip on the spinal cord, reflexes can become overly snappy and hyperactive.

question: Which group of blood pressure medications must be strictly avoided during pregnancy because they can harm the baby's kidneys?

options.A: Beta-blockers
options.B: Calcium channel blockers
options.C: ACE inhibitors
options.D: Centrally acting alpha agonists

explanation: Remember: ACE inhibitors are known to mess with how a baby's kidneys develop, so doctors steer clear of them during pregnancy.

question: A patient with uncontrolled diabetes insists on a strict all-day fast. What is the major clinical risk to watch for?

options.A: Chronic deficiency of essential fatty acids
options.B: Rapid weight gain due to metabolic slowdown
options.C: Sudden accumulation of excess dietary calcium
options.D: Severe blood sugar fluctuations and dangerous hypoglycemia

explanation: Going long hours without food while taking diabetes medications puts the patient at high risk for a dangerous drop in blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Keep a close eye on them!

question: A patient from a local community frequently visits the clinic complaining of severe body aches and fatigue, but medical tests find no physical cause. What should the nurse consider?

options.A: Physical complaints can never be linked to psychological stress
options.B: The patient is definitely fabricating symptoms to get prescription drugs
options.C: The laboratory equipment is likely malfunctioning and needs calibration
options.D: The patient might be expressing emotional distress through physical symptoms

explanation: Many individuals culturally communicate psychological distress through physical symptoms, requiring nurses to look beyond pure medical lab results. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h4)

question: What protective layers wrap around both the brain and the spinal cord?

options.A: Meninges
options.B: Ventricles
options.C: Myelin sheaths
options.D: Synapses

explanation: The meninges are like sturdy cushion layers wrapped around your delicate central nervous system for safety. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h3)

question: You are cleaning a utility room that has broken glass and used syringes. Which protective gear do you need most?

options.A: An ordinary cloth mask and rubber slippers
options.B: Heavy utility gloves and protective eyewear
options.C: Soft examination gloves and plastic shoes
options.D: A sterile white gown and a surgical cap

explanation: You got it! Thick utility gloves protect your hands from cuts and punctures, while eyewear keeps any accidental splashes of dirty fluids out of your eyes.

question: Why do doctors give tocolytic drugs to a mother in preterm labour?

options.A: To delay delivery for 48 hours to give steroids time to work
options.B: To permanently stop uterine contractions for the rest of the pregnancy
options.C: To cure any underlying bacterial infection causing the labour
options.D: To lower the mother's blood pressure back to normal levels

explanation: Think of tocolytic drugs as our 'pause button'—they buy crucial hours so life-saving steroids can help the baby's lungs. You are thinking like a real nurse!

question: What is the main goal of 'triage' during an emergency response?

options.A: To collect donations from onlookers gathered at the disaster scene
options.B: To register the personal identification numbers of all displaced victims
options.C: To quickly sort casualties by injury severity so the most urgent get treated first
options.D: To determine who caused the disaster through a formal investigation

explanation: Spot on! Triage helps medical teams quickly spot who needs life-saving care right this second so nobody who is critical gets left behind.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier keeping men away from health clinics?

options.A: Staff attitudes that treat men as unwelcome intruders
options.B: Clinics operating convenient evening and weekend hours
options.C: Long waiting times that clash with work schedules
options.D: Facility environments focused solely on mothers and babies

explanation: Convenient operating hours would actually encourage attendance, whereas the other options represent real barriers men face. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h5)

question: Why must you be extra, extra careful when doing nail care for a patient with diabetes?

options.A: The soap used for soaking can cause immediate chemical burns
options.B: Diabetic nails grow much faster than normal nails
options.C: Diabetic patients are allergic to standard metal nail clippers
options.D: Nerve damage and poor circulation increase infection and ulcer risks

explanation: You've got this! Because diabetes can cause poor blood flow and nerve damage (neuropathy), even a tiny nick can easily turn into a dangerous, slow-healing ulcer.

question: How does palliative care view the dying process?

options.A: As a medical failure that must be avoided
options.B: As a punishment for past misdeeds
options.C: As a condition that can always be reversed
options.D: As a normal and natural part of life

explanation: Palliative care philosophy regards dying as a normal human process that neither hastens nor postpones death. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h2)

question: How does fluid in the chest cavity (pleural effusion) make it hard to breathe?

options.A: Fluid enters the alveoli and destroys the natural surfactant
options.B: It blocks the main windpipe and chugs off air supply
options.C: Fluid physically presses against the lung, stopping it from expanding fully
options.D: It forces the heart to beat too fast, causing sudden shock

explanation: You got it! The fluid takes up space in the chest and squeezes the lung from the outside, so it can't puff up nicely when breathing in.

question: A community health nurse notices an increase in diarrhea cases during the rainy season. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Educating local families on safe water storage and oral rehydration
options.B: Ordering advanced genetic testing for all community members
options.C: Recommending immediate surgical procedures for every household
options.D: Waiting for patients to arrive at the central hospital for intravenous therapy

explanation: Simple community education on clean water and oral rehydration saves lives quickly and stops outbreaks right at the source.

question: What is the primary role of autotrophic microbes in natural water bodies?

options.A: Increasing water turbidity and cloudiness
options.B: Causing severe water-borne infections
options.C: Performing photosynthesis to produce oxygen
options.D: Dissolving heavy metals in the sediment

explanation: Autotrophic microbes contain chlorophyll and produce oxygen just like land plants, supporting aquatic life. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h2)

question: Why do advanced emphysema patients often end up with a flattened diaphragm and hard-working breathing muscles?

options.A: Scar tissue in the pleural lining pulls the diaphragm upward into the neck
options.B: Loss of pulmonary blood flow weakens the intercostal muscle fibers
options.C: Thick mucus plugs block the trachea and force the chest wall to expand
options.D: Air trapping hyperinflates the lungs and pushes the diaphragm downward

explanation: Makes total sense! Trapped air keeps the chest inflated like a balloon, flattening the diaphragm and making it tired and less efficient. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which human factor frequently causes industrial accidents in the workplace?

options.A: Strict adherence to international building codes
options.B: Regular maintenance of old electrical grids
options.C: Operator fatigue and bypassed safety checks
options.D: Excessive routine safety training for workers

explanation: Well done! When workers are exhausted or skip safety rules to save time, accidents are much more likely to happen.

question: Which stage of change describes a person who has not yet considered changing an unhealthy habit?

options.A: Action
options.B: Maintenance
options.C: Preparation
options.D: Precontemplation

explanation: In the precontemplation stage, the person isn't even thinking about changing yet, and might not even see that there is a problem. Spotting these stages is a key nursing skill you are mastering easily!

question: Why do we say a resident's care plan must be treated as a living document?

options.A: It is legally required to be rewritten word-for-word every single morning.
options.B: It is only used during the initial admission interview and never again.
options.C: It must be adjusted whenever the resident's clinical condition changes.
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to document daily shift assessments.

explanation: A resident's health changes day by day, so their care plan needs to grow and update right along with them. Spot on!

question: What is the standard time frame following the end of a pregnancy for a death to be classified as a maternal death?

options.A: Within 6 months
options.B: Within 7 days
options.C: Within 42 days
options.D: Within 1 year

explanation: A maternal death includes any death occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days following the termination of the pregnancy, provided it is related to the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h1)

question: Why do some sleeping pills sometimes fail to give patients truly refreshing rest?

options.A: They permanently damage the brainstem respiratory control centers
options.B: They cause severe dehydration and electrolyte imbalance during sleep
options.C: They distort normal sleep stages by suppressing deep and rapid eye movement sleep
options.D: They cause the patient to sleep for less than two hours per night

explanation: Certain sleeping pills mess with your natural sleep cycle, blocking you from getting enough of that crucial deep sleep and REM rest.

question: Why should nurses always focus on 'felt needs' (real problems the community faces daily) when planning education?

options.A: It guarantees immediate financial funding from donors
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to prepare visual aids
options.C: Learners pay closer attention to problems they actually experience
options.D: Government policy requires ignoring community complaints

explanation: People naturally care more about health issues affecting their everyday lives than abstract or distant theories.

question: Which residential model features 24-hour staff presence for high support?

options.A: Self-contained private flats
options.B: Supervised hostels
options.C: Temporary weekend shelters
options.D: Transitional living facilities

explanation: Well done! Supervised hostels have staff around the clock to give extra guidance to residents who still need help with daily routines and medications.

question: Who played the primary role in introducing Western-style nursing and hospitals to Nigeria during the colonial era?

options.A: Missionary societies
options.B: Military combat units
options.C: International trade unions
options.D: Local traditional rulers

explanation: Christian missions established the earliest Western hospitals and introduced formal nursing concepts to Nigeria. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: What does 'pharmacokinetics' actually mean?

options.A: The financial cost of manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: The chemical structure of a synthetic compound
options.C: How a medication binds to specific cellular receptors
options.D: What the body does to a drug through absorption and excretion

explanation: Think of pharmacokinetics as the journey of the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. You can master this!

question: What is the best immediate action for the nurse to take after the nebulizer cup runs dry?

options.A: Reassess lung sounds and measure the patient's oxygen saturation
options.B: Immediately start a second dose of medication without waiting
options.C: Disconnect the air flow meter and leave the room quietly
options.D: Instruct the patient to lie flat in bed for one hour

explanation: Checking lung sounds and oxygen levels right after treatment confirms whether the bronchodilator opened the airways successfully. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h6)

question: As a nurse, what is the very first thing you do after a patient's test comes back positive?

options.A: Discharge the patient to home isolation
options.B: Interview the index patient to find contacts
options.C: Vaccinating the entire neighborhood immediately
options.D: Closing down public markets in the local area

explanation: Spot on! We start by talking to the main patient (the index case) to gently find out who they've been hanging out with recently.

question: Which health benefit comes directly from regular physical education in schools?

options.A: Prevention of childhood obesity and improved motor skills
options.B: Immediate cure for congenital heart defects
options.C: Permanent enhancement of visual acuity
options.D: Complete elimination of infectious respiratory diseases

explanation: Correct! Staying active helps kids burn energy, build strong bones and muscles, and improve their coordination.

question: A nurse is discharging a patient who had a bowel obstruction from Crohn's disease. Which symptom should the nurse flag as an urgent emergency?

options.A: Feeling tired during normal daily physical activities
options.B: Mild gas and bloating after eating a small meal
options.C: Severe, unrelenting abdominal pain and persistent vomiting
options.D: A slight increase in daily bowel movement frequency

explanation: Never ignore severe, worsening pain and constant vomiting—they can signal a returning blockage or a serious bowel injury. You're becoming a great nurse!

question: If you want to know if smoking status (smoker vs. non-smoker) is linked to chronic bronchitis, which test should you use?

options.A: Chi-Square test of independence
options.B: Chi-Square goodness-of-fit test
options.C: Repeated measures ANOVA
options.D: Independent samples t-test

explanation: Spot on! Because we are looking for a relationship between two categorical variables (smoking status and bronchitis status), the test of independence is the right pick.

question: Which type of supervision focuses mainly on helping a nurse learn new skills and grow?

options.A: Normative supervision
options.B: Punitive supervision
options.C: Formative supervision
options.D: Restorative supervision

explanation: Think of 'formative' like 'forming' or building your skills. It's educational and helps you grow into a more competent nurse.

question: Which stage of the schistosome life cycle can directly infect humans?

options.A: Sporocysts
options.B: Miracidia
options.C: Cercariae
options.D: Eggs

explanation: Cercariae are the free-swimming little swimmers released by snails into the water. When they touch human skin, they dive right in! You've got this.

question: What makes pulmonary arteries unique compared to most other arteries in the body?

options.A: They operate under very high pressure
options.B: They carry deoxygenated blood
options.C: They contain multiple valves to prevent backflow
options.D: They transport blood toward the body organs

explanation: While almost all other arteries carry oxygenated blood to the body, pulmonary arteries are unique because they carry deoxygenated blood away from the heart to the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which food group is the body's main and quickest source of energy?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Proteins
options.C: Fats
options.D: Vitamins

explanation: Carbs break down quickly into glucose, which acts as the favorite fuel for your cells and brain.

question: A patient comes in with a metal flake stuck on the surface of their eye. Why is irrigation a good choice here?

options.A: Fluid pressure forces the metal deeper to hide the pain
options.B: Washing the eye replaces the need for a physical eye exam
options.C: Irrigation completely dissolves metal on contact
options.D: The fluid stream can safely flush away loose surface irritants

explanation: Spot on! If something is just resting loosely on the surface, a gentle, steady flow of liquid is a safe way to float it right out.

question: What is the primary role of calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D produced by the kidneys?

options.A: Stimulating red blood cell maturation
options.B: Increasing systemic blood pressure
options.C: Regulating blood glucose concentrations
options.D: Promoting calcium absorption in the gut

explanation: Calcitriol helps maintain strong bones by ensuring adequate dietary calcium is absorbed from the intestines. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why do misplaced endometrial implants cause ongoing pain and scarring in the pelvis?

options.A: They grow rapidly into malignant tumors within weeks
options.B: They release massive amounts of male hormones into the abdomen
options.C: They bleed during each cycle, causing local inflammation and adhesions
options.D: They destroy the nerves supplying the lower abdominal wall

explanation: Wherever these misplaced cells land, they still respond to monthly hormones by trying to 'bleed'. This trapped blood irritates nearby tissue, causing painful inflammation and sticky scar tissue.

question: A newborn baby experiences a sudden drop in blood oxygen levels shortly after delivery. Which foetal shunt is most likely to remain open or reopen due to this stress?

options.A: The ductus arteriosus
options.B: The umbilical vein
options.C: The ductus venosus
options.D: The portal sinus

explanation: Low oxygen levels and respiratory distress in a newborn can keep the muscular ductus arteriosus open or cause it to dilate. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h6)

question: At 20 weeks pregnant, a patient's serum creatinine level is 1.0 mg/dL. What does this result suggest?

options.A: Severe maternal dehydration
options.B: Normal kidney function for pregnancy
options.C: Potential underlying renal impairment
options.D: A normal non-pregnant baseline

explanation: Because kidney filtration speeds up during pregnancy, normal creatinine levels actually drop below 1.0 mg/dL. A value of 1.0 mg/dL means the kidneys might not be clearing waste as well as they should right now.

question: When studying how patients cope with long-term illness, why are interviews often better than rigid surveys?

options.A: Interviews allow participants to explain things in their own words
options.B: Surveys are too expensive to print out in hospital wards
options.C: Interviews do not require any ethical review board approval
options.D: Surveys only work when patients are unconscious

explanation: Spot on! People aren't checkboxes. Letting patients talk freely gives you rich insights that a standard survey would completely miss.

question: Which type of vaccine contains a weakened form of a live germ?

options.A: Inactivated
options.B: Live-attenuated
options.C: Recombinant
options.D: Toxoid

explanation: Spot on! 'Live-attenuated' means a living germ has been weakened (attenuated) so it can safely spark a strong immune response.

question: During a vaginal exam, you suddenly spot an umbilical cord prolapse. What is your very first emergency action?

options.A: Manually lift the presenting part off the cord to relieve pressure
options.B: Send the patient home to rest until the next scheduled clinic visit
options.C: Administer oral pain medication and document the finding later
options.D: Wait quietly for the next contraction to see if the cord recedes

explanation: Every second counts here! By using your hand to lift the baby's head off the cord, you keep oxygen flowing to the baby until delivery.

question: Which gland contributes the largest proportion of fluid volume to semen?

options.A: Prostate gland
options.B: Seminal vesicles
options.C: Testes
options.D: Bulbourethral glands

explanation: The seminal vesicles provide about 60% of the total fluid volume found in an ejaculate. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T3#GNS121_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the main goal of therapeutic drug monitoring?

options.A: To confirm that the medication is producing the desired clinical effect
options.B: To test if the patient is secretly selling their prescription
options.C: To ensure the pharmacy department bills the patient correctly
options.D: To prove that the physician chose the cheapest available brand

explanation: We monitor to make sure the drug is actually helping the patient heal and not causing trouble. Spot on!

question: What is a key nursing duty during the disaster preparedness phase?

options.A: Conducting community education and hazard awareness training
options.B: Demolishing unsafe buildings before an earthquake occurs
options.C: Writing national disaster budget legislation
options.D: Importing foreign medical equipment without authorization

explanation: Well done! Getting ready means educating the public so everyone knows what to do before an emergency strikes.

question: When is the right time for a nurse-midwife to practice hand hygiene in the labor ward?

options.A: Only at the beginning of the morning shift
options.B: Only after touching visible blood or amniotic fluid
options.C: Before and after every patient contact
options.D: After finishing all clinical duties for the day

explanation: Simple and non-negotiable: wash your hands or use sanitizer before and after every single patient touch to keep infections away.

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for rectal medication administration?

options.A: Mild high blood pressure
options.B: Mild headache and body fatigue
options.C: History of seasonal allergies
options.D: Recent rectal or bowel surgery

explanation: Inserting a suppository into a healing surgical site can damage tissue, cause pain, and disrupt sutures. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T18#GNS125_U3_T18_h6)

question: What is the main risk of aggressively stripping surgical drainage tubes?

options.A: It can create a strong vacuum that damages delicate internal tissue
options.B: It always causes the collection container to crack and leak fluid
options.C: It permanently ruins the plastic so it can no longer collect blood
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling any post-operative surgical pain

explanation: Stripping generates high negative pressure inside the tube, which can suck delicate tissue into the drainage holes and cause injury or bleeding. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h3)

question: Why should a nurse always measure height and weight accurately instead of just guessing?

options.A: Inaccurate numbers can lead to dangerous errors in medication dosing
options.B: Patients get offended if the nurse guesses their size
options.C: Estimated numbers make the patient chart look untidy
options.D: Hospital management requires exact figures for billing purposes only

explanation: Many strong drugs, especially for children and critically ill patients, depend on exact body measurements so you don't accidentally give too much or too little. Great job learning the safety rules!

question: How did the invention of psychotropic drugs change the daily job of a psychiatric nurse?

options.A: It shifted their focus from physical containment to rehabilitation and therapy
options.B: It increased the frequency of using physical restraints and seclusion
options.C: It forced nurses to spend most of their shifts performing surgeries
options.D: It eliminated the need for any direct patient interaction or observation

explanation: Once medications could control severe symptoms, nurses could finally stop just guarding doors and start doing meaningful therapeutic work with patients!

question: According to public health standards, what does reproductive health truly focus on?

options.A: Eliminating all infectious diseases affecting only adult women
options.B: Physical, mental, and social well-being in all matters of the reproductive system
options.C: Controlling population growth through strict laws
options.D: Ensuring every family has at least four children

explanation: Think of reproductive health as a total package! It's not just about avoiding disease or planning family size—it's about a person's overall physical, mental, and social well-being regarding their reproductive system. You've got this!

question: A clinic is near a busy highway and a river that floods easily. Who should nurses prioritize first when planning an evacuation?

options.A: Elderly patients with mobility limitations and infants in the pediatric ward
options.B: Young administrative staff members who drive their own private cars to work
options.C: Healthy adult visitors waiting at the outpatient reception lobby
options.D: Off-duty nurses resting in the staff common room upstairs

explanation: Always save those who cannot help themselves first. Babies and immobile elders rely entirely on nurses to get them to safety!

question: Which of these is an example of a favorable expense variance for a hospital ward?

options.A: Spending less money on operational supplies than what was originally budgeted
options.B: Purchasing expensive broken equipment that requires immediate replacement
options.C: Experiencing a sudden drop in total patient admissions and revenue
options.D: Paying significantly higher overtime wages to staff than planned

explanation: A variance is 'favorable' when you spend less money than you expected while still keeping standards high. Good job staying under budget!

question: Why is a predictable daily routine important in a half-way house?

options.A: It promotes stability and reduces anxiety for residents
options.B: It replaces the need for any medication or therapy
options.C: It ensures that nurses have less paperwork to complete
options.D: It punishes residents who wake up late in the morning

explanation: Great thinking! Structure and predictability help individuals with mental health conditions feel secure, calm, and organized.

question: Which of these is one of the most common types of errors in clinical practice?

options.A: Intentionally falsifying nursing charts
options.B: Anesthesia overdoses during routine scans
options.C: Medication errors
options.D: Deliberate patient abandonment

explanation: Giving or managing medications happens all day, every day in nursing, which makes medication errors one of the most frequent types of clinical mistakes.

question: When a nursing manager has to settle a dispute between two departments, what should be their main goal?

options.A: Collaborative problem-solving and patient safety
options.B: Ignoring the issue until it resolves on its own
options.C: Punishing the staff members who started the argument
options.D: Closing one of the departments involved

explanation: Spot on! Good leaders look for the root cause and solve problems together, always keeping patient safety at the heart of it all.

question: Why is it important for nurses to know the difference between the incubation period and the latent period?

options.A: Symptoms always start at the exact same hour infectiousness begins
options.B: Latent periods only apply to non-infectious chronic illnesses
options.C: Incubation periods tell nurses when to discharge patients
options.D: A person may be able to spread the disease before showing any symptoms

explanation: Exactly! Sometimes the latent period is shorter than the incubation period, meaning someone can spread an infection while still feeling completely well.

question: Why are bedside nurses considered central to hospital quality assurance?

options.A: They are responsible for hospital budget approvals
options.B: They spend the most time directly caring for patients
options.C: They write all the medical textbooks in the country
options.D: They alone have the power to hire new doctors

explanation: You know it! Because you are right there at the bedside 24/7, you are in the best position to catch safety gaps and make care better.

question: Which healthcare professional often acts as the central coordinator in palliative care teams?

options.A: The nurse
options.B: The pharmacist
options.C: The hospital administrator
options.D: The laboratory scientist

explanation: That's you! Because nurses spend the most time right at the bedside, we are the glue holding the care team and the family's communication together.

question: What factor most commonly drives teenagers toward dangerous, underground abortion practices?

options.A: Abundant availability of free clinical termination services
options.B: Encouragement from community health committees
options.C: Complete legal protection for all medical procedures
options.D: Strict social stigma, legal restrictions, and lack of safe care access

explanation: Exactly. When judgment, strict laws, and a lack of open support block safe care, desperate teenagers unfortunately turn to risky alternatives.

question: What is the function of the flexible plastic canulas used in an MVA kit?

options.A: To seal the outside opening of the vagina during suction
options.B: To travel through the cervix and vacuum out uterine tissue
options.C: To measure the exact internal temperature of the uterus
options.D: To pump local anesthetic pain medicine into the cervix

question: Why do we call smooth muscle 'involuntary'?

question: How do a person's cultural and spiritual beliefs usually affect how they grieve?

question: How can we best describe public health surveillance?

options.A: A method for punishing clinics that lose patient files
options.B: A financial audit of private clinic expenditures

question: Before physically transporting a patient for an external referral, what crucial step must the nurse or doctor complete?

question: What is the main difference between mechanical and biological vector transmission?

question: Which condition features flashbacks, avoiding reminders, and being constantly on edge long after a disaster?

question: Why do maternity homes hold clinical audits and review close-calls?

question: Why is mixing a chemical disinfectant to the correct ratio so important?

question: Why can't a nurse officially diagnose a patient with diabetes based on just one high random blood sugar test?

options.B: Blood sugar levels never stay high for long periods

question: What is the main goal of a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) after something goes wrong in the hospital?

question: Why does someone struggling with long-term drug use need larger doses over time to get the same high?

question: If a patient stays in bed for a very long time due to a degenerative disease, what happens to their joints and muscles?

question: A patient with severe burn wounds is at risk of poor healing if which nutritional goal is missed?

question: Why is it so important to involve the family when setting rehabilitation goals?
