options.C: Line graph
options.D: Flow chart

explanation: You got it! Bar charts are awesome for comparing different groups side-by-side, like different wards in your hospital.

question: A newborn with severe moulding and a large cephalhematoma is in the nursery. Which nursing action is WRONG and unsafe?

options.A: Observing the skin closely for developing yellow discoloration
options.B: Encouraging gentle feeding and assessing for sucking strength
options.C: Monitoring vital signs and neurological status frequently
options.D: Attempting to massage the pooled blood away from the skull bone

explanation: Spot on! Massaging a cephalhematoma or moulded skull is dangerous because it can cause more bleeding and tissue damage. Hands off the swelling!

question: Why is knowing a patient's home region and geography useful for a nurse?

options.A: It shows their exact genetic makeup.
options.B: It predicts their exact household income.
options.C: It explains why certain nutritional deficiencies appear in specific areas.
options.D: It helps choose where to build new hospitals.

explanation: Geography shapes what food is available locally, which directly connects to why certain health issues or malnutrition patterns show up in specific regions.

question: Which fungal infection is a major cause of meningitis in patients with advanced HIV/AIDS seen in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Sporotrichosis ulcers
options.B: Cryptococcal meningitis
options.C: Aspergillus pneumonia
options.D: Dermatophyte ringworm

explanation: Correct! Cryptococcal meningitis is a serious opportunistic infection in immunocompromised patients, and spotting it early saves lives on the wards.

question: Why must metformin be withheld from patients receiving an iodine contrast agent?

options.A: To stop the contrast dye from crystallizing inside the stomach lining
options.B: To keep the patient's blood pressure from dropping too low during the test
options.C: To prevent the dangerous buildup of lactic acidosis if kidneys struggle
options.D: To ensure the x-ray machine captures a clear picture of the pancreas

explanation: If the contrast temporarily impairs kidney function, metformin can accumulate and trigger a severe metabolic complication called lactic acidosis. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the most common cause of anaemia in pregnant women everywhere?

options.A: Vitamin B12 deficiency
options.B: Autoimmune destruction
options.C: Acute blood loss
options.D: Iron deficiency

explanation: You nailed it. Because the growing baby and placenta need a lot of iron, mothers can easily run low if their diet or supplements don't keep up.

question: What should a cataract surgery patient wear while sleeping during early recovery?

options.A: A rigid protective eye shield
options.B: A dark pair of polarized sunglasses
options.C: A sterile moist gauze dressing
options.D: A tight elastic pressure bandage

explanation: Wearing a hard shield to bed ensures the patient doesn't accidentally rub or press on their healing eye while fast asleep.

question: What is the best nursing action when family members are scared of casual contact with an HIV-positive relative?

options.A: Prescribe prophylactic antibiotics for everyone living in the house
options.B: Report the family to social welfare for discriminatory behavior
options.C: Provide clear education on how the virus is actually transmitted
options.D: Advise the patient to move out to protect the relatives

explanation: Spot on! Clearing up myths with gentle facts helps chase away fear and stops unnecessary separation at home.

question: What does a Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment primarily look at?

options.A: Occupational history and retirement savings
options.B: Physical, functional, psychological, and social well-being
options.C: Surgical fitness for emergency organ transplants
options.D: Childhood developmental milestones

explanation: A Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment looks at the whole person—not just physical symptoms, but how they function, their mood, and their social life too.

question: What does medical confidentiality require of a nurse caring for an HIV-positive patient in Nigeria?

options.A: Keeping the patient's test results private and sharing them only with explicit consent
options.B: Reporting the patient's name to local community leaders immediately
options.C: Posting the diagnosis on the hospital notice board for staff awareness
options.D: Disclosing the status to the patient's employer during routine checks

explanation: Patient confidentiality is a sacred professional duty, ensuring health details are never shared without permission. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h8)

question: When a mistake happens, why does a systems thinker look beyond the person who made it?

options.A: To prove that the nursing staff had too many tasks to complete
options.B: To find a way to replace human workers with automated machines
options.C: To understand how the environment and processes allowed the error
options.D: To make sure the hospital avoids paying any financial penalties

explanation: Blaming an individual often hides the real structural and environmental weaknesses that let the error happen in the first place. Every nurse makes mistakes; looking at the system helps us fix the root cause so you can practice safely!

question: What is a major benefit of continuous antenatal risk assessment?

options.A: Complete prevention of all natural labor pains
options.B: Early detection of potential complications before labor starts
options.C: Guaranteeing that the baby will be born on a specific day
options.D: Removing the need for traditional birth attendants entirely

explanation: Catching warning signs early allows the healthcare team to act before a minor issue becomes an emergency. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h2)

question: What does the 'planning' function of management involve?

options.A: Punishing staff members for clinical errors
options.B: Deciding ahead of time what needs to be done and who will do it
options.C: Ordering medical supplies from external vendors
options.D: Evaluating individual lab results at the bedside

explanation: Planning is simply looking ahead, setting goals, and figuring out your game plan before the shift gets crazy.

question: Which of these is an example of a moist-heat cooking method?

options.A: Broiling
options.B: Poaching
options.C: Roasting
options.D: Grilling

explanation: Poaching involves gently submerging food in hot liquid right below boiling point. Delicious and tender!

question: What makes a home-based care plan different from a hospital care plan?

options.A: It focuses only on physical ailments and ignores mental health
options.B: It relies entirely on high-tech electronic equipment
options.C: It must fit the everyday resources and lifestyle of the family
options.D: It is written by the family members without professional input

explanation: Home care plans must be practical and realistic for the client's home environment to ensure lasting success. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h5)

question: A 16-year-old girl visits the clinic showing signs of severe mood swings and sudden weight loss. What should you, as the nurse, suspect first?

options.A: Emerging psychosocial or mental health challenges typical of this age group
options.B: Normal age-related cognitive decline
options.C: Permanent physical disability from birth
options.D: Early onset geriatric syndrome

explanation: Well done! Teens experiencing emotional stress often show it through sudden changes in behavior, body image concerns, or physical symptoms. Always keep an eye out for their mental wellbeing.

question: Which signs point toward acute bacterial prostatitis turning into a dangerous systemic infection (urosepsis)?

options.A: Gradual hair loss across the chest and abdomen
options.B: Low resting heart rate and warm, dry skin
options.C: Painless swelling of the bilateral ankle joints
options.D: High fever, rigors, and severe perineal pain

explanation: Look out for red flag infection signs! Severe shaking chills (rigors), high fever, and intense pelvic pain mean the infection is spreading systemically.

question: What does Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) measure?

options.A: Calories used solely to digest a heavy meal
options.B: Total calories burned during intense physical exercise
options.C: Energy burned by the body at complete rest for vital functions
options.D: The speed at which the stomach empties into the intestines

explanation: BMR measures the baseline energy required to keep you alive while resting quietly. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h5)

question: What do we call it when blood collects inside the pleural space?

options.A: Pneumothorax
options.B: Empyema
options.C: Hemothorax
options.D: Pleural effusion

explanation: You got it! 'Hemo' means blood and 'thorax' means chest, so blood in the chest cavity is a hemothorax.

question: As a nurse, what is an important rule to remember when checking in on a traumatized patient?

options.A: Rely solely on written questionnaires handed out at the triage desk
options.B: Ignore non-verbal cues and focus entirely on laboratory values
options.C: Insist that the patient describe every frightening moment in detail
options.D: Avoid forcing the patient to recount traumatic details immediately

explanation: Spot on! Never pressure a survivor to retell a scary story before they are ready. Pushing too hard can actually re-traumatize them. Let them take their time. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h4)

question: When a local disaster strikes, who is almost always the very first responder?

options.A: International humanitarian workers
options.B: Specialized military rescue squads
options.C: Local community members themselves
options.D: Federal disaster relief agencies

explanation: You got it! Neighbors and local residents are already right there to help before official rescue teams arrive.

question: What is the main protective job of antioxidants found in fruits and vegetables?

options.A: Neutralizing unstable free radicals that damage cells
options.B: Acting as direct hormones to lower blood pressure
options.C: Speeding up the mechanical digestion of dietary fats
options.D: Providing the main structural foundation for muscle tissue

explanation: Correct! Antioxidants fight off unstable free radicals so they don't damage our cells and DNA.

question: Clinic records show few malaria cases, but local medicine vendors report selling lots of malaria drugs daily. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the clinic staff to the ministry for failing to do their jobs
options.B: Use community-based data collection like household surveys to find the real disease burden
options.C: Assume the medicine vendors are lying and close down their shops
options.D: Conclude that malaria has been completely eradicated in that area

explanation: Not everyone goes to the government clinic first; many buy drugs across the counter. To find the true picture, nurses must look beyond clinic logbooks and talk to the community directly.

question: During embryonic folding, a portion of the yolk sac is tucked inside to form which vital structure?

options.A: Amniotic cavity
options.B: Neural tube
options.C: Cardiovascular system
options.D: Primitive gut tube

explanation: Spot on! This folded tissue becomes the starting point for the baby's digestive tract, known as the primitive gut tube.

question: Which condition means a patient must NEVER be given misoprostol?

options.A: Well-managed gestational diabetes
options.B: Mild iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: A history of high blood pressure
options.D: A confirmed ectopic pregnancy

explanation: Misoprostol cannot treat a pregnancy outside the uterus. Giving it would dangerously delay emergency surgery. Always check for this first!

question: How would you simply define a 'nursing theory'?

options.A: A strict set of disciplinary rules for student nurses
options.B: A proven drug recipe used in emergency rooms
options.C: An organized set of concepts explaining a phenomenon
options.D: A list of hospital equipment costs for the year

explanation: Correct! A theory gives us a helpful framework to explain why things happen and guides our nursing actions.

question: What does the Infant Mortality Rate measure?

options.A: Babies who die before reaching their first birthday
options.B: Children under five years old who get malaria
options.C: Mothers who die during childbirth
options.D: Total number of babies born in a hospital

explanation: Infant Mortality Rate specifically tracks deaths occurring during the first year of life per one thousand live births. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why do droplet precautions only need a regular surgical mask instead of an N95?

options.A: Droplets are heavy, travel short distances, and do not linger in the air
options.B: Droplets evaporate instantly before reaching any healthcare worker
options.C: Droplets can only pass through skin pores, not through cloth
options.D: Surgical masks filter out microscopic floating particles better than N95s

explanation: Exactly! Large droplets quickly drop down rather than floating, so a simple surgical mask gives you all the protection you need for close care.

question: Which clinical sign tells you right away that a patient has an upper airway blockage rather than a lower airway problem?

options.A: Expiratory wheezing
options.B: Bilateral basal crackles
options.C: Intercostal recession
options.D: Inspiratory stridor

explanation: Stridor is that high-pitched sound you hear when breathing in, usually pointing to a narrowed upper airway like the larynx or trachea.

question: What is the main goal of doing a mental status examination during a home visit?

options.A: To measure the client's physical strength and reflexes
options.B: To test the client's long-term memory from childhood
options.C: To evaluate the current cognitive and psychological functioning of the client
options.D: To diagnose the exact subtype of personality disorder

explanation: You got it! The mental status exam gives us a quick, structured snapshot of how the patient is thinking and behaving right now.

question: Why are nurses legally responsible for the medications they give to patients, even if a doctor prescribed them?

options.A: Pharmacies lack the legal power to sue clinical staff for mistakes.
options.B: Nurses must share equal financial blame with the hospital owners for drug errors.
options.C: Doctors expect nurses to take full legal blame if a drug reacts poorly.
options.D: Nurses are ultimately responsible for any independent action they take at the bedside.

explanation: You've got this! Even though a doctor writes the prescription, as the nurse at the bedside, you have a duty to double-check that the drug is safe before giving it.

question: What is the main job of pulmonary surfactant inside the tiny air sacs (alveoli)?

options.A: To stimulate the diaphragm to contract during inspiration
options.B: To warm incoming air before it reaches the bronchioles
options.C: To transport oxygen directly into the bloodstream
options.D: To lower surface tension and prevent alveolar collapse

explanation: You've got this! Surfactant acts like a special coating that reduces surface tension inside the tiny air sacs, keeping them open and stable so breathing is easy. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T9#GNS213_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe home environment practice for a patient with Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Ensuring hallways and stairwells have bright, even lighting
options.B: Installing secure grab bars in the bathroom and shower
options.C: Clearing pathways of electrical cords and clutter
options.D: Placing loose decorative throw rugs over slick tile floors

explanation: Watch out for loose rugs! Because Parkinson's patients often shuffle their feet, throw rugs are a major tripping hazard that should always be removed.

question: When should a nurse use surgical asepsis instead of medical asepsis?

options.A: Assisting a patient with a bed bath
options.B: Feeding a patient who has a stroke
options.C: Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter
options.D: Taking routine vital signs in the morning

explanation: Inserting a urinary catheter enters a sterile body cavity, requiring surgical asepsis to prevent introducing bacteria into the bladder. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h2)

question: How often should temperature checks typically be performed on individuals in quarantine?

options.A: Twice daily
options.B: Every hour around the clock
options.C: Only when they feel hot
options.D: Once a week

explanation: Checking temperature twice daily helps catch early signs of fever before symptoms worsen. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is creating a warm, non-judgmental environment so essential in family planning nursing?

options.A: It guarantees that no client will ever experience any side effects
options.B: It encourages clients to be honest and seek care without fear
options.C: It forces every community member to use the exact same method
options.D: It eliminates the need for any documentation in client files

explanation: When clients feel safe and unjudged, they tell the truth about their health and keep coming back for care. That is the heart of nursing!

question: What is the main idea behind efficiency in healthcare?

options.A: Increasing the total number of private hospitals in urban areas
options.B: Reducing the number of patients admitted to emergency wards
options.C: Maximizing health benefits using the fewest possible resources
options.D: Ensuring that all medical staff receive equal monthly salaries

explanation: Efficiency is all about making the most of what we have without wasting precious resources or money.

question: How do active muscle movements during AROM help with blood circulation?

options.A: They make the arteries much wider and longer permanently.
options.B: They remove all red blood cells from the lower extremities.
options.C: They act as a physical pump pushing blood back toward the heart.
options.D: They completely stop the heart from beating too fast.

explanation: Think of the muscles as a natural pump! As they squeeze, they push blood back up toward the heart against gravity, keeping clots away.

question: In many poor communities, what is the main dietary cause of micronutrient deficiencies?

options.A: High intake of dairy products and fresh vegetables
options.B: Frequent eating of high-protein animal meals
options.C: Heavy reliance on a single starchy staple food
options.D: Excessive consumption of imported canned foods

explanation: Correct! Eating only one starchy food day in and day out means the body misses out on the wide variety of nutrients it needs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h3)
